newsitem.title: USA: Mexico allows its banks to trade CME products - CME.
newsitem.headline: Mexico allows its banks to trade CME products - CME.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) said it has received notification that the Banco de Mexico has authorized Mexican banks to trade Mexican IPC stock index futures and options listed on CME.
The authorization followed earlier approvals for Mexican institutions to trade the CME's peso and Brady bond contracts, the exchange added.
"This action reflects the strong relationships we have built with officials in Mexico over the past several years," CME Chairman Jack Sandner said in a statement.
CME listed the derivatives on Mexico's blue-chip IPC (Indice de Precios & Cotizaciones) index .MXX last May as part of its Growth and Emerging Markets sector.

"We look forward to participation by the Mexican banks and broker-dealers in our IPC futures and futures options," CME President Bill Brodsky said in a statement. "The banks' active use of our peso contract has contributed to its tremendous success."
